messages:
Evan: Layover debate: espresso shot in terminal or try to nap for 45m? Which actually makes you more functional on arrival?
Mina: Espresso wins for me every time. Short nap + caffeine is the combo.
Diego: I vote nap if the flight was overnight. Otherwise espresso.
Tanya: 45m naps are the worst. They leave you groggy. If you can do 20m power nap then sure.
Evan: Good point. Power nap sounds doable at gate. Any tips for napping at terminals (no recline)?
Mina: neck pillow + eye mask + white-noise app. Also move to a quieter concourse.
Diego: Wear layers so you don’t wake up freezing. And set two alarms.
Tanya: Pro tip: book a lounge pass for a few hours on long layovers. Quiet, plugs, and decent coffee later. Worth it for midday connect.
travel-bot: FYI: Airport lounges often have day passes from $25-$65 depending on carrier/partner. Check your cc perks! :robot_face:
Evan: Anyone used airport sleep pods? Are they overrated?
Mina: Used one in AMS. Small but private. Bring socks and they provide blanket. Great for 90m.
Diego: Overrated for short layovers (time to check-in/out). Great if you have 3+ hours.
Tanya: Poll time: espresso+no nap / espresso+20m nap / 45m nap / lounge pass — react with emoji to vote
Evan: ":coffee:" for espresso no nap
Mina: ":coffee::zzz:" for espresso + 20m
Diego: ":zzz:" for 45m nap
Tanya: ":airplane_small:" for lounge pass
Evan: Also PSA: keep chargers in your jacket pocket when trying to sleep at gate. Worst feeling is waking up with 2% battery.
Mina: And mark your bag with a ribbon or bright sticker. Makes it easy to spot if you doze off.
Diego: Meme: "me: I’ll just rest my eyes for 20 minutes
also me: sleeps through boarding" (image)
Tanya: Ok final note: if you’re transiting international -> domestic, leave extra time for customs. Don’t rely on a 45m buffer.
Evan: Solid. Thanks y’all. I’m leaning espresso+20m. See you at the offsite — will bring granola bars for the gate squad. :yum:"
